gazetteer_names_needed.name: Lower Styria
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Slovene Styria (Spodnja Stajerska), the part of the duchy now in northern Slovenia: Maribor, Ptuj, Celje; about 6,000 km2. Replaced in the dossier by a 45 km radius round Maribor plus the Celje municipality.

gazetteer_names_needed.name: Celje
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: Celje (Cilli), Slovenia, about 15.27E 46.23N; only an admin1 municipality exists in the gazetteer, no place entry.

gaps.what: Whether any part of Lower Styria (Maribor, Ptuj, Celje) belonged to the duchy before 1456; the base outline before 1456 is Steiermark only

1487-1491: Cliopatria draws Hungary over all of Styria and drops it from the House of Habsburg; the pages opened name only Mautern in Styria (1481) and the Archbishopric's fortresses (1479), and have Frederick fleeing to Graz in 1487; no event entered
1502-1918 outline and any territorial change besides the 1918-19 loss of the southern third of Lower Styria (undated inside 1918-1919)
Border parcels at the 1254 Hungarian transfer ('large parts of Styria' yielded to Bela IV, undated) and the later Habsburg gains and losses at the edges
Ruler list after Ferdinand II (1637); the WebFetch extract of the page list ends there

problems: All five Cliopatria 'Duchy of Styria' shapes are wrong (verdict wrong): 1260-1271 is a Styria-sized polygon (16,888 km2) lying in Tyrol (62 of 67 cells) and western Carinthia, none in Steiermark; 1272-1501 are one to eight cells in the Friuli/Gorizia/Tolmin borderland, the 1450 shape having the same bbox as Cliopatria's Patriarchate of Aquileia 1422-1449 outline (Aquileia row ends 1449, this starts 1450). eu-13 (Aquileia) and whoever writes Tyrol should know.

Styria's real land is drawn in Cliopatria under other rows: Kingdom of Bohemia 1260-1278 (62-66 cells), House of Habsburg 1279-1486 and 1492-1515 (64-66 cells), Kingdom of Hungary 1487-1491 (all 67 cells), Habsburg Monarchy from about 1520. The dossier makes Styria a state of its own, so the orchestrator must choose between rendering it as a separate colour inside those rows or as a union partner/vassal tint of the holder; the bohemia, house-of-habsburg and habsburg-monarchy dossiers should not draw it twice. If the partition is preferred, keep this dossier for 1180-1259 and its ledger only.

Life span differs from Cliopatria's 1260-1501: the page gives 1180 (raised to duchy) and 1918 (crown land of Austria-Hungary dissolved). 1502-1918 rests on one page and can be cut at 1806 if wanted; no invented dissolve at 1501 was written.

Dynasty and holder changes (1192, 1254, 1260, 1276, 1379, 1457, 1564, 1619, 1804, 1867) are rename events, so the dossier has 10 renames, 1 gain, 1 found, 1 dissolve; the only territorial gain is the 1456 Celje inheritance (confidence 2, region approximated by a radius round Maribor plus Celje).

The Duchy of Styria article is thin (no area, no boundary, no section headings) and WebFetch returns summarised extracts, so some quotes in notes stop mid-sentence; the 5-page budget is spent (Duchy of Styria, Ottokar II of Bohemia, Counts of Celje, Austrian-Hungarian War 1477-1488, Matthias Corvinus). The war and Matthias pages do not support a Hungarian occupation of Styria in 1487-1491.
Only one state was assigned to eu-09-b; no other dossier was written or edited.
